top.summary: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence A Chinese state-run newspaper has denied that Beijing had any link to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair. The Global Times , a nationalist tabloid, said American outlets, in particular the New York Times, were “going crazy” with speculative stories. “All it took were a few photographs showing Asian faces and Nvidia’s previous efforts to push for relaxing trade curbs on China. “This is precisely how American media, which have long styled themselves as ‘objective,’ manufacture stories.” Asian equity markets are rallying this morning after Wall Street’s rebound on Friday, although concerns surrounding an internal investigation involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang are capping gains. The company is down around -3.5% on platforms that provide weekend prices. Continue reading...

One of them was only because I caught a passing postman on a parcel round who arranged one just for me. The bundle contained a bank card, two notifications of an overdue bill I was unaware of, a weeks-old letter from my new water company asking me to set up payments, and a letter about a routine cancer test. Sports.title: Ramla Ali wins first world titles at 36 with highly controversial split decision
Sports.summary: British-Somali boxer claims first world titles in Texas Kreps outlands Ali but loses disputed split decision Baumgardner wins 135lb belt as Dubois feud heats up Australia’s Nicolson retains junior featherweight title British-Somali boxer Ramla Ali became a world champion for the first time at the age of 36 on Sunday night after escaping with a highly contentious 10-round split decision over former sparring partner Mikiah Kreps to claim the vacant WBO and IBF women’s junior featherweight titles in Arlington, Texas. Ali, who grew up in east London after fleeing Somalia’s civil war with her family and went on to become the first boxer to represent the African country at the Olympics, completed her remarkable journey to the top of the 122lb division at College Park Center on her second attempt at a world championship – but only after a controversial verdict rewarding her for a fight that appeared to be largely controlled by her opponent. Here’s what to watch this evening 9pm, BBC Two A still unresolved story of institutional failure and relentless campaigning, this documentary explores the damage done to generations of children by sodium valproate, a drug that was licensed for prescription to people with epilepsy despite concerns having arisen after testing. At the heart of the story are Janet Williams and Emma Murphy, two mothers who refused to be deterred by official inertia (and, at times, outright scorn) and whose robust lack of self-pity makes this film stirring rather than dispiriting. Culture.title: ‘Thicky thicky dumb dumb’ satirist Cody Dahler on his viral videos: ‘my material is presented to me on a silver platter!’
Culture.summary: The writer and podcaster on why politics is made to seem more complicated than it is and his mission to unpack world events for everyone Why did you get into comedy? My mum was a professional dancer and always encouraged me to perform. Given that I have zero rhythm, comedy was my other option. She wrote me a poem called Mrs Brown’s Moggy, about a cat that was often very soggy, for my school’s talent show. Because you can’t tell the difference between real and polite laughter at the age of six, I assumed I’d killed my first gig and convinced myself I was born to do nothing else. Where do you find your material? In a world where Robert Jenrick claims Nigel Farage has “ probably done more than almost anybody to stand against racism ”, the answer is that my material is presented to me on a silver platter each morning.
